design.text: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled (imiglucerase) non-inferiority, multicenter study in patients switching from enzyme replacement therapy

citations.quote: Trial 2 was a randomized, open-label, active-controlled, non-inferiority, multicenter clinical study evaluating the efficacy and safety of CERDELGA compared with imiglucerase in 159 treated GD1 patients (median age 37.4 years) previously treated with enzyme replacement therapy

population.text: Adult GD1 patients previously treated with ≥3 years of enzyme replacement therapy who met pre-specified therapeutic goals at baseline

citations.quote: previously treated with enzyme replacement therapy (\ge 3 years of enzyme replacement therapy, dosed at 30-130 U/kg/month in at least 6 of the prior 9 months) who met pre-specified therapeutic goals at baseline.

endpoint.text: Primary composite endpoint: stability in all four domains (hemoglobin level, platelet count, liver volume, spleen volume) between baseline and 12 months

citations.quote: The primary composite endpoint required stability in all four component domains (hemoglobin level, platelet count, liver volume, and spleen volume) based on changes between baseline and 12 months.

n.text: N=159 treated patients (randomized 2:1 CERDELGA vs imiglucerase)

citations.quote: non-inferiority, multicenter clinical study evaluating the efficacy and safety of CERDELGA compared with imiglucerase in 159 treated GD1 patients
One hundred sixty (160) patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to treatment with eliglustat (n=106) or Cerezyme (n=54).

result.text: CERDELGA met non-inferiority to imiglucerase: 84.8% of CERDELGA patients met the primary composite endpoint vs 93.6% imiglucerase; lower bound of 95% CI of the 8.8% difference was -17.6%, within the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -25%.

citations.quote: the percentage of patients meeting the primary composite endpoint was 84.8% for the CERDELGA group compared to 93.6% for the imiglucerase group. The lower bound of the 95% CI of the 8.8% difference, -17.6%, was within the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -25%.

indication.text: Long-term treatment of adult patients with Gaucher disease type 1 (GD1) who are CYP2D6 extensive metabolizers (EMs), intermediate metabolizers (IMs), or poor metabolizers (PMs) as detected by an FDA-cleared test

citations.quote: CERDELGA is indicated for the long-term treatment of adult patients with Gaucher disease type 1 (GD1) who are CYP2D6 extensive metabolizers (EMs), intermediate metabolizers (IMs), or poor metabolizers (PMs) as detected by an FDA-cleared test [*see Dosage and Administration (2.1)*].

target_moa.text: Eliglustat is a specific inhibitor of glucosylceramide synthase (IC50 = 10 ng/mL), acting as substrate reduction therapy to reduce accumulation of glucosylceramide (GL-1) that occurs in GD1 due to acid β-glucosidase deficiency.

citations.quote:
CERDELGA is a specific inhibitor of
glucosylceramide synthase (IC_{50} = 10 ng/mL), and acts as a substrate reduction therapy
for GD1.
Gaucher disease is caused by a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme acid \beta-glucosidase.
Cerdelga (eliglustat tartrate), a SRT, is a new molecular entity. It is a member of a novel class of glucosylceramide (GL-1) synthase inhibitors that resembles the ceramide substrate for the enzyme.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% across Trials 1 and 2) were fatigue, headache, nausea, diarrhea, back pain, pain in extremities, and upper abdominal pain. In Trial 1, arthralgia (45% vs 10% placebo) and headache (40% vs 30%) were most frequent. Key safety concern is QTc/PR/QRS prolongation with high eliglustat exposure from drug-drug interactions.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 10\%) are: fatigue, headache, nausea, diarrhea, back pain, pain in extremities, and upper abdominal pain (6.1)
Arthralgia	9 (45)	2 (10)

Eliglustat is a CYP2D6 and CYP3A substrate. Drugs that inhibit CYP2D6 and CYP3A metabolism pathways may significantly increase the exposure to eliglustat and result in prolongation of the PR, QTc, and/or QRS cardiac intervals that could result in cardiac arrhythmias

detail.text: An FDA-cleared test for determining CYP2D6 genotype is required to select patients (EMs, IMs, PMs); CYP2D6 genotype testing is essential for safe and effective use.

citations.quote: CYP2D6 genotype testing is essential for the safe and effective use of eliglustat. FDA-cleared tests are available for genotyping CY
